reason: Section 12 covers several distinct by-law passage rules: ordinary validity requirements, metric conversion revisions, official-language substitution by-laws, and meeting, amendment and voting mechanics.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Ordinary validity requirements for municipal by-laws
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 12(1) states the ordinary readings, publication alternative, seal, signature and enactment statement needed for a by-law to be valid.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the ordinary readings, publication alternative, seal, signature and enactment statement required for a valid municipal by-law.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Metric-conversion by-law revision validity requirements
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 12(1.1) separately states validity requirements for a by-law revising measurements from Canadian units to the International System of Units.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the special validity requirements for a by-law that only revises measurements to International System units.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Official-language substitution by-laws and pre-third-reading amendment
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 12(1.2) and 12(1.3) address by-laws that substitute or add an official-language version and permit amendment before third reading without further filing.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the special validity and amendment rules for by-laws that substitute or add an official-language version.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: By-law readings, amendment before third reading, voting thresholds and saving rule
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 12(2) to 12(5) cover emergency readings, amendment before third reading, two-thirds or whole-council votes, meaning of whole council and protection of earlier by-laws.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the meeting, amendment, voting-threshold, whole-council and saving rules for passing by-laws.

reason: Section 13 is one conflict rule making this Act, regulations or Orders in Council prevail over conflicting charters or private or special Acts, while allowing regulations to extend municipal powers from those instruments.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Conflict with municipal charters or private or special Acts

evidenceText: extend the powers of a municipality

proposedGroups.reason: The target states priority in a conflict and the regulation power to extend municipal powers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what prevails when this Act conflicts with a municipal charter or private or special Act and how charter powers may be extended.

reason: Section 14 is too broad for one unit because it covers Cabinet structural-change powers, who may institute or petition for proceedings, dissolution studies and limits, classification after changes, and regulation-making criteria.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Cabinet powers for incorporation, amalgamation, annexation, decrement and rural community conversion
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 14(1) to 14(1.4) set the Lieutenant-Governor in Council’s structural-change powers, legislative or resolution requirements for amalgamations and contiguous-area grouping rules.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Cabinet powers and consent or contiguity rules for municipal incorporation, amalgamation, annexation, decrement and rural community conversion.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Institution, petitions and studies for structural-change or dissolution proceedings
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections identify Minister, council, rural community council and resident petitions, interim council status after rural community incorporation, dissolution studies, special-Act dissolution limits and petition qualification dates.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who may start or petition for municipal structural-change proceedings and how dissolution studies and petition dates work.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Incorporation as town, city or municipality after amalgamation or annexation
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 14(5) and 14(5.1) address incorporation as a town or city after amalgamation or annexation and mandatory incorporation after rural community amalgamation with municipalities.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an amalgamated or annexed area may be incorporated as a town, city or municipality.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulations on conditions, procedures and criteria for structural changes
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 14(7) separately authorizes regulations respecting conditions, procedures and criteria for listed municipal structural changes.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation power over conditions, procedures and criteria for municipal structural changes.

reason: Section 14.1 is repeal-only and contains no current operative study content.
Section 15 is one town-incorporation rule allowing incorporation of a village as a town on Minister recommendation if population and service-level conditions are met.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Village incorporation as town based on population and services

evidenceText: population of fifteen hundred or more

proposedGroups.reason: The target states the two conditions for incorporating a village as a town.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a village may be incorporated as a town.

reason: Section 15.1 separates the condition and appointment path for dissolving a town or village into a rural community from the regulation contents and additional criteria powers for the dissolution.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Dissolution of town or village into rural community and appointed persons
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 15.1(1) to 15.1(4) define ratepayer, authorize dissolution by regulation after a feasibility report or study, and allow appointment of persons to carry out dissolution actions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a town or village may be dissolved into a rural community and who may be appointed to carry out dissolution actions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulation contents for town or village dissolution
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 15.1(5) lists what the dissolution regulation may provide, including rural community status, assets, liabilities, ratepayer obligations, tax rates, by-laws, services, claims, property vesting, notice and incidental acts.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what matters a regulation dissolving a town or village may provide for.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulations on conditions, procedures and criteria for becoming rural community
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 15.1(6) separately authorizes regulations on conditions, procedures and criteria before a town or village may become a rural community or part of one.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation power over conditions, procedures and criteria for a town or village becoming a rural community.

reason: Section 16 is a single city-incorporation rule allowing a town with population of ten thousand or more to be incorporated as a city.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Town incorporation as city based on population

evidenceText: population of ten thousand or more

proposedGroups.reason: The target states the population condition for incorporating a town as a city.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a town may be incorporated as a city.

reason: Section 17 is one continuity rule keeping the mayor and council in office as the mayor and council of the new municipality until a new council is elected and takes office.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mayor and council continuity after incorporation change

evidenceText: mayor and the council in office
until a new council has been elected

proposedGroups.reason: The target states who holds office after a village becomes a town or a town becomes a city.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who serves as mayor and council after a village is incorporated as a town or a town as a city.

reason: Section 18 is one evidentiary rule making an Order in Council conclusive evidence of compliance with conditions precedent and due incorporation or boundary change.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Order in Council as conclusive evidence for municipal structural change
proposedGroups.reason: The target states the evidentiary effect of an Order in Council effecting incorporation, amalgamation, annexation or decrement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what an Order in Council proves for municipal incorporation, amalgamation, annexation or decrement.

reason: Section 19 is a long structural-change implementation provision with distinct topics for definitions, Order in Council contents, affected-municipality transition, first-council powers and finances, officer transition, information/time/conflict rules, and affected-area adjustments.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Definitions for affected municipality and new municipality in structural-change orders
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 19(0.1) defines affected municipality, council of an affected municipality and new municipality for the section.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the definitions of affected municipality, council of an affected municipality and new municipality for structural-change orders.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Order in Council contents for incorporation, amalgamation, annexation or decrement
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 19(1) lists what an Order in Council may prescribe or provide, including name, boundaries, wards, planning designations, assets and liabilities, local commissions, first elections and incidental matters.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what an Order in Council may provide when effecting municipal incorporation, amalgamation, annexation or decrement.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Affected council office, candidacy, day-to-day powers and void actions before effective date
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 19(2) to 19(5) address affected council terms, no by-elections, candidacy for first council, limits on affected council actions and voidness of contravening actions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how affected municipal councils and their members operate when a first election occurs before the effective structural-change date.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: First council appointments, transitional budget, advances and early by-law powers
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 19(6) to 19(8) address first-council officer appointments, transitional budget, procedure by-laws, new-municipality expense treatment and Minister of Finance advances.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the first council’s appointment, transitional budget, procedure by-law and advance-funding powers before the effective date.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: First council by-law review, estimates, collective agreements and officer transition
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 19(9) to 19(9.4) address by-law review, new by-laws, estimates, tax rate, collective agreements, officer appointments, officer revocation or reassignment, effective dates, voting threshold and service of resolutions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the first council’s powers over by-laws, estimates, collective agreements, officers and related resolutions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Information duties, time adjustments, conflict rules and affected-area adjustments
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 19(10) to 19(18) cover information requests, Minister time adjustments, conflict-of-interest protections, annexation or decrement without first election, affected-area planning and boundary adjustments, non-application rules and rural community application.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the information, time-adjustment, conflict, no-first-election, affected-area adjustment and rural-community application rules in section 19.
